mainTopic: Learning from a rule that was itself learned through a היקש (the תודה breads), and whose view sets the midnight deadline for eating the פסח
overview: The גמרא first gives another answer to an earlier problem: the outside blood placements (חוץ) are learned from the inside ones (פנים) in one single learning, not as a chain. It then shows that the view that a rule learned through a היקש plus another source is not a היקש fits the drasha on "תביאו". That drasha models the תודה bread on שתי הלחם: one עשרון per loaf, though not a total of two עשרונים, because of "תהיינה". The מצה loaves then get the same ten עשרונים through a היקש to the חמץ loaves. For the other view, the גמרא answers that "תביאו" is an extra word, so only one היקש is used. Next, רב יוסף says the משנה's rule that the פסח is eaten only until midnight follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, who learns it from "בלילה הזה" and מכת בכורות. רבי עקיבא disagrees: the deadline is the time of haste, and "בלילה" teaches only that the פסח is eaten at night. אביי suggests midnight may be just a rabbinic fence, but רב יוסף proves from the word "only" that it is Torah law. The פרק איזהו מקומן then ends.

steps.title: Outside is learned from inside in one learning
steps.stepSummary: Another answer: חוץ is learned from פנים all at once, not in two separate stages.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say instead: the outside rule is learned from the inside rule in one single learning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different answer to the problem it was just discussing. It says there is only one learning here, not a chain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that it looked like one learning was built on top of another. This answer says the outside blood placements (חוץ) are learned straight from the inside ones (פנים) in one move. Since there is no chain, the problem of learning from something that was itself learned does not come up.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say: introduces another answer
Outside: the blood placements on the outer altar
Inside: the blood placements done inside the היכל
All at once, in one single learning
Is learned or derived

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
outside is learned from inside all at one time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the problem discussed just before this section.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changes how the learning works: one single learning instead of a chain
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It looked like the outside rule came from a rule that was itself learned, so it would be learning from something already learned.
steps.terutzMaskana: חוץ is learned straight from פנים in one step, so there is no chain.

steps.title: Setting up: the view that it is not a היקש fits the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says that according to the view that it is not a היקש, the פסוק about the wave bread makes good sense. This sets up a question on the other view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, according to the one who says it is not a היקש, that is why the פסוק says: "From your dwellings you shall bring wave bread."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move with a "בשלמא": one view fits well with a פסוק. That hints the other view will have trouble with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A "בשלמא" line says that something works nicely for one side. The question on the other side usually comes right after. Here the גמרא first brings the פסוק and its drasha, and the challenge itself comes in step 7.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, it works well for: the first half of a challenge
According to the one who says
Learning one thing from another because the Torah places them side by side
Wave bread: the שתי הלחם of שבועות

steps.confusionAlert: The "בשלמא" is only half of the question. Don't expect the challenge to finish here; the גמרא first brings the drasha, and only in step 7 says what is difficult for the other view.

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who says
it is not a juxtaposition,
this is why it is written:
“From your dwellings you shall bring wave bread” –

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the answer about חוץ and פנים to the related argument over whether such a learning counts as a היקש.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that it does count as a היקש (the challenge itself comes in step 7)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק and its drasha fit the view that it is not a היקש, which suggests a problem for the other view.

steps.title: The bread of the תודה is modeled on שתי הלחם
steps.stepSummary: The drasha learns from the extra word "תביאו" that bread brought from elsewhere, the תודה bread, is made like שתי הלחם: one עשרון per loaf.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק did not need to say "you shall bring." So why does it say it? To teach that anything you bring from another place is like this. Just as there each loaf takes one tenth, here too each loaf takes one tenth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the drasha on the פסוק it just cited. The word "תביאו" teaches that other bread offerings are made like שתי הלחם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "תביאו" looks extra, so it is used to teach something new. Bread "from another place" is compared to שתי הלחם. Because each of the two loaves takes one עשרון of flour, each loaf of the תודה also takes one עשרון.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse says: points to the wording of a פסוק
A tenth of an איפה, a measure of flour
A loaf
Just as there, so too here: the comparison formula

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source that each loaf of the תודה uses one עשרון of flour.

phrases.english: For the verse did not need to say “you shall bring,”
so why does the verse say “you shall bring”?
Anything that you bring
from another place
phrases.notes: The word in round brackets is in the standard גמרא, but the corrected wording leaves it out. This is talking about the bread brought with the תודה.

phrases.english: is like this;
just as there, a tenth for each loaf,
so too here, a tenth for each loaf.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the drasha on the פסוק quoted in the בשלמא.
steps.raayaObject: That the bread of the תודה follows the model of שתי הלחם

steps.title: Should the תודה bread also total only two tenths?
steps.stepSummary: The drasha asks: if the comparison holds, maybe the total flour of the תודה should also be just two עשרונים.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then just as there it is two tenths in total, here too it should be two tenths?!
steps.whatsHappening: The drasha challenges itself: if we copy שתי הלחם, why not copy the total amount too?
steps.deeperAnalysis: שתי הלחם use two עשרונים in total, one for each loaf. A full comparison would also limit the total for the תודה bread to two עשרונים, even though it has many more loaves.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Two tenths in total

phrases.english: If so – just as there it is two tenths,
so too here, two tenths?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes the comparison from step 3 further than intended.
steps.kashyaTarget: How far the comparison between the תודה bread and שתי הלחם reaches
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the bread is "like this," maybe every detail carries over, including the total amount.

steps.title: "תהיינה" limits the total to שתי הלחם
steps.stepSummary: The word "תהיינה" teaches that only שתי הלחם total two עשרונים; the comparison does not carry over the total.
steps.whatsHappening: The drasha answers its own question from the word "תהיינה" in the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "They shall be" points to these two loaves alone. So only the amount per loaf is copied to the תודה, not the total of two עשרונים.

keyTerms.meaning: They shall be: a limiting word

steps.whatToRemember: The תודה loaves copy שתי הלחם in the amount per loaf (one עשרון each), but not in the total of two עשרונים. That total is limited by "תהיינה".

phrases.english: The verse says: “they shall be.”
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:17. The word limits the total of two tenths to those two loaves alone.

steps.terutzResolutionType: A limiting word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תודה bread would also total only two עשרונים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only שתי הלחם total two עשרונים; the תודה bread copies just the amount per loaf.

steps.title: The מצה loaves of the תודה are matched to the חמץ loaves
steps.stepSummary: The ten חמץ loaves need ten עשרונים, and the פסוק 'על חלת לחם חמץ' teaches that the מצה is brought to match the חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: We already learned that the leavened loaves need ten עשרונים. Where do we learn the same for the מצה? The פסוק says 'with loaves of leavened bread', which means: bring מצה to match the leavened bread.
steps.whatsHappening: The drasha finishes its point. Once the חמץ loaves are set at ten עשרונים, it uses a פסוק to give the מצה loaves the same amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ten עשרונים for the חמץ loaves came from two sources together: the comparison to שתי הלחם and the פסוק that sets ten loaves. For the view that something learned through a היקש plus another source is not counted as a היקש, the חמץ amount may teach the מצה through a new היקש. That completes the בשלמא from step 2; the next step asks how the other view can accept it.

keyTerms.meaning: A tenth of an איפה, a fixed measure of flour
Leavened bread brought with the תודה
Corresponding to, matching
The פסוק teaches, introducing a source

phrases.english: And we have learned ten for the leavened bread;
phrases.notes: 'Ten' means ten עשרונים of flour, one for each loaf, learned from 'תביאו' in step 3.

phrases.english: ten for the matza, from where do we know it?
The verse says: 'With loaves of leavened bread'
Bring matza to match the leavened bread.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the drasha after step 5 limited the comparison, now extending the amount from the חמץ to the matza.
steps.raayaObject: That the matza loaves of the תודה also total ten עשרונים
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 7:13, 'על חלת לחם חמץ', read as a היקש of matza to חמץ

steps.title: A problem for the view that it counts as a היקש
steps.stepSummary: For the view that something learned partly through a היקש counts as a היקש, how can the מצה be learned from the חמץ?
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the one who says it is a היקש, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the drasha it just finished. It asks how it can work according to the other opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule that something learned through a היקש cannot be used to teach another thing through a second היקש. If the חמץ loaves got their amount from שתי הלחם by a היקש, then using the חמץ to teach the מצה would be a היקש built on a היקש, which is not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: A comparison drawn because two things are placed together in the תורה
According to the one who says
What is there to say? A sign of a real difficulty

phrases.english: But according to the one who says it is a juxtaposition,
phrases.notes: The word 'not' in round brackets is in the standard גמרא, but the corrected wording leaves it out, so read it as 'it IS a היקש'.

phrases.english: what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: אלא למאן דאמר הוי היקש מאי איכא למימר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the step 6 derivation according to the second view set up in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The step 6 derivation of the matza amount from the חמץ
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the חמץ amount came from a היקש, a second היקש from it (to the matza) is not allowed.

steps.title: 'תביאו' is an extra word, so there is no היקש on a היקש
steps.stepSummary: The link between שתי הלחם and the תודה comes from the extra word 'תביאו', not from a היקש, so the מצה can be learned from the חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'You shall bring' is an extra word.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge in one short line. The first link was never a היקש; it came from an extra word in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An extra word works as if the תורה had written the rule directly about the תודה loaves. So the חמץ amount counts as written outright, and the one היקש from the חמץ to the מצה is the first and only היקש.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You shall bring', the word in the פסוק of שתי הלחם
Extra, an added word that comes to teach something

steps.whatToRemember: The flour for the תודה breads comes from an extra word ('תביאו') plus one היקש. That way it works even for the view that something learned through a היקש cannot teach through another היקש.

phrases.english: 'You shall bring' is extra.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Changes the source: the first link is an extra word, not a היקש
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חמץ loaves got their amount from שתי הלחם by a היקש, so they could not teach the matza.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first link comes from an extra word, so only one היקש is used.

steps.title: Who taught that the פסח is eaten only until midnight?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule about the קרבן פסח and asks which תנא it follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The פסח is eaten only...' Who is the תנא?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic starts. The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that the פסח is eaten only at night until midnight, and asks whose view this is. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every תנא agrees that the פסח must be finished by midnight. So the גמרא wants to know which opinion the משנה follows.

keyTerms.meaning: The Pesach offering, eaten on the night of the 15th of ניסן
Who is the תנא? Asking whose view a משנה follows
Midnight

phrases.english: The Paschal offering is eaten only...
phrases.notes: This quotes the start of the משנה's line: the פסח is eaten only at night, until midnight.

phrases.english: Who is the tanna?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the תודה breads and opens a new topic from the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that the פסח may be eaten only until midnight

steps.title: רב יוסף: it is רבי אלעזר בן עזריה
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the משנה follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: it is רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the question by naming the תנא. The proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Naming the תנא tells us the midnight limit is one opinion, not something everyone agrees on.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
It is Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב יוסף רבי אלעזר בן עזריה היא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.

steps.title: 'This night' is compared to the night of מכת בכורות
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה learns 'בלילה הזה' by the פסח from 'בלילה הזה' by מכת בכורות: just as that lasted until midnight, so does eating the פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says: it says here 'on this night', and it says there 'And I will pass through the land of Egypt on this night'. Just as there it was until midnight, so too here it is until midnight.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove רב יוסף's answer. In it, רבי אלעזר בן עזריה learns the midnight limit through a matching phrase in two פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same words, 'בלילה הזה', appear for eating the פסח and for מכת בכורות. מכת בכורות happened at midnight, so the night for eating the פסח also ends at midnight. This is a גזירה שוה, learning one place from another through the same wording.

keyTerms.meaning: Learning one law from another through matching words in the תורה
'On this night', the shared phrase
Just as there, so too here: carries the rule over

steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק 'And I will pass through Egypt' itself does not say 'midnight'. That detail comes from another פסוק about מכת בכורות (שמות 11:4).
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the rule that the קרבן פסח, according to רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, must be eaten before midnight.

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Elazar [ben Azarya] says:
It is stated here: 'On [that] night',
and it is stated there:
'And I will pass through the land of Egypt on that night';
just as there it was until midnight,
so too here it is until midnight.

steps.triggerLanguage: דתניא רבי אלעזר בן עזריה אומר נאמר כאן בלילה הזה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב יוסף's answer in step 10 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אלעזר בן עזריה limits eating the פסח to midnight
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with a גזירה שוה from 'בלילה הזה' (שמות 12:8 and 12:12)

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: The פסח may be eaten until the time of haste
steps.stepSummary: Inside the ברייתא, רבי עקיבא challenges רבי אלעזר בן עזריה. The פסוק says the פסח is eaten 'in haste,' which means it may be eaten until the time of haste, not only until midnight.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said to him: But hasn't it already been said, 'And you shall eat it in haste'? That means until the time of haste!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues. רבי עקיבא now argues against רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's 'until midnight' rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה connected 'this night' to מכת בכורות, which happened at midnight. רבי עקיבא points to a different word, 'in haste.' The time of haste was when the Jews rushed out of מצרים, so the deadline stretches until then and not just until midnight.

keyTerms.meaning: But hasn't it already been said? (an opening that brings a פסוק as a challenge)
In haste
The time of haste, when the Jews hurried out of מצרים

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said to him,
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, from the previous step.

phrases.english: But hasn't it already been said:
"And you shall eat it in haste"
meaning until the time of haste!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, וַהֲלֹא כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's reading of the פסוק inside the same ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's 'until midnight' deadline
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A different word in the Torah, 'in haste,' points to a later deadline: the time of haste.

steps.title: Then why does the Torah say 'on this night'?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks a question on רבי עקיבא's view: if 'in haste' sets the deadline, what do the words 'on this night' teach?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the verse say 'on this night'?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges רבי עקיבא. If he does not use 'this night' for the midnight rule, those words seem to have no job. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every word in the Torah should teach something. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה used 'on this night' to learn midnight. Once רבי עקיבא rejects that, he must explain what the phrase teaches instead.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if your view is right)
Why does the verse need to say this?
On this night

phrases.english: If so,
why does the verse say "on this night"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי עקיבא's reading from the previous step.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's 'until the time of haste' reading
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'in haste' sets the deadline, the words 'on this night' would seem to teach nothing.

steps.title: 'At night' teaches that the פסח is eaten at night and not by day
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי עקיבא, 'on this night' teaches that the פסח, unlike other קדשים, is eaten at night and not during the day.
steps.simpleTranslation: For I might have thought it is like all the offerings that are eaten by day. So the verse says 'at night': it is eaten at night, and it is not eaten by day.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers for רבי עקיבא. The phrase 'on this night' still has a job: it tells us when the eating starts, not when it ends.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most קדשים are eaten starting from the day they are brought. Without the פסוק, we might think the same of the פסח. 'At night' teaches that the פסח is eaten only at night, so רבי עקיבא does not need this phrase for a midnight deadline.

keyTerms.meaning: For one might have thought
Sacrificial offerings
Therefore the verse says

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה: the פסח may be eaten until midnight, learned from 'this night' and מכת בכורות. רבי עקיבא: until the time of haste, and 'this night' teaches only that it is eaten at night and not by day.

phrases.english: For I might have thought it is like all the offerings
that are eaten by day;
so the verse says "at night":
at night it shall be eaten,
and it is not eaten by day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of the previous step.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the phrase a different job
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The words 'this night' would be useless for רבי עקיבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: They teach that the פסח is eaten at night and not by day, unlike other קדשים.

steps.title: אביי: Maybe the משנה's midnight is only a rabbinic fence
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב יוסף: why assume the משנה follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה and means Torah law? It could follow רבי עקיבא, with midnight as a rabbinic rule to keep people away from sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: And from where do you know it follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה and is Torah law? Perhaps it is rabbinic, to keep people far from sin!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רב יוסף's claim from Step 10. אביי questions whether the ברייתא really proves it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both a Torah rule and a rabbinic fence would produce the same words in the משנה: 'until midnight.' A midnight cutoff fits רבי עקיבא too, if the רבנן set it early so people do not eat past the real Torah deadline. So the משנה alone does not show it follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do you know?
By Torah law
By rabbinic law
To keep a person far from sin (a protective fence)
Perhaps

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying רבי אלעזר בן עזריה is wrong. He is only saying the משנה could fit רבי עקיבא too, if midnight is just a rabbinic safety line.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
phrases.notes: He is talking to רב יוסף, who said the משנה follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.

phrases.english: And from where do you know it follows Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya,
and is Torah law?
Perhaps it is rabbinic,
and meant to keep people far from sin!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the ברייתא to challenge רב יוסף's claim from Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that the משנה follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A midnight cutoff could be a rabbinic fence that fits רבי עקיבא, so the משנה does not prove whose view it follows.

steps.title: The word 'only' shows the midnight rule is Torah law
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers from the משנה's wording 'only until midnight.' It matches the other 'only' rules of the פסח in the same משנה. Just as those are Torah law, so is midnight.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what does 'only until midnight' mean? Rather, it is like there: just as there it is Torah law, so here too it is Torah law.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף defends his claim using the exact words of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the פסח, the משנה lists several rules in the same 'only' style. The 'only until midnight' rule sits in that list, so it should be the same kind of rule as the others. Since the others are Torah law, midnight is Torah law too, and that is רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's view.

steps.title: הדרן — Closing the פרק איזהו מקומן
steps.stepSummary: This is the closing formula for the פרק איזהו מקומן.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, איזהו מקומן.
steps.whatsHappening: The פרק ends here, with the traditional closing line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is not part of the argument. It marks the end of the פרק and expresses the hope to come back and learn it again.
